html:
The Falklands War was a ten-week war between Argentina and the United Kingdom in 1982 over the Falkland Islands, which Argentina calls the Malvinas, in the South Atlantic.

Argentina had long claimed the islands, held by Britain since 1833. On 2 April 1982 the military junta of General Leopoldo Galtieri, facing economic crisis and protest, invaded them, expecting Britain not to fight. Margaret Thatcher sent a naval task force 13,000 kilometres south. A British submarine sank the cruiser General Belgrano, killing over 300 sailors, and Argentine planes sank several British ships. British troops landed and took the capital, Stanley, on 14 June.

About 650 Argentines and 255 British died. The defeat discredited the junta, which gave way to elections in 1983, ending the Dirty War. In Britain the victory strengthened Thatcher. Argentina still claims the islands, and the war is remembered in its streets and in the Maradona goals against England in 1986.
sum: The Falklands War was a ten-week war between Argentina and the United Kingdom in 1982 over the Falkland Islands, which Argentina calls the Malvinas, in the South Atlantic.
